findings.title: CTF Flag Extracted — Role Injection + 2FA Bypass
findings.description: The Flask login endpoint sets session['role'] from the user-supplied POST parameter instead of the database-stored role. An attacker can authenticate as emp/emppassword but POST role=admin, granting admin session without 2FA. Additionally, the 2FA code is hardcoded to '1234' and can be completely bypassed. The FLAG environment variable is then revealed in the admin dashboard.
findings.tool_used: manual HTTP exploitation + source code review

reproduction.command: 1) POST /login: username=emp&password=emppassword&role=admin → session with role=admin\n2) Access GET /admin/dashboard with that session → flag revealed in flag=\"\" attribute
